newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-CZECHS NAME SQUAD FOR KEY WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CZECHS NAME SQUAD FOR KEY WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: Czech coach Dusan Uhrin on Wednesday named a 19-player squad for next week's key World Cup qualifier against Yugoslavia, sticking mainly to the lineup that propelled the Czechs to the Euro 96 finals.
Fourteen members of the Euro 96 team were chosen to represent the Czechs, who badly need a win to keep pace with the rest of the Group Six pack.

Spain leads the group with 13 points after five matches, followed by the Yugolsavs on 12 points in five matches. With nine points in four matches, Slovakia is also ahead of the Czechs who have four points in three games, including a 1-0 loss in Belgrade in November.
"Everybody knows what's riding on this game, and the players have promised to player with the unity and strength that we showed in England last summer," Uhrin said.
"We know that that success is in the past though, and must look to the future," he added.
Uhrin's biggest concern remains his attack, which has failed to pressure opposing defences throughout the qualifying round.

Sparta Prague's Vratislav Lokvenc has been called up for his first CAP in over a year to replace the ageing Radek Drulak, who continues to lead the Czech first division scoring race despite a winter break transfer to FC Linz in Austria.

Liverpool's Patrik Berger will be relied upon heavily to control play, especially in the midfield, while Manchester United's Karel Poborsky is showing signs of returning to form after a disappointing stretch in the Premiership.
The Czech Premiership connection stretches as far back as the goal, with Uhrin expecting to start West Ham United goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko over the more experienced Newcastle keeper Pavel Srnicek.
"A week ago I saw Miklosko play...and he was in great form," added assistant coach Ivo Viktor.
Goalkeepers - Ludek Miklosko (West Ham United), Pavel Srnicek (Newcastle United)
Defenders - Miroslav Kadlec (Kaiserslautern), Jan Suchoparek (Racing Strasbourg), Michal Hornak (Sparta Prague), Tomas Repka (Sparta Prague), Karel Rada (Sigma Olomouc)

Midfielders - Radek Bejbl (Atletico Madrid), Karel Poborsky (Manchester United), Radoslav Latal (Schalke 04), Jiri Nemec (Schalke 04), Patrik Berger (FC Liverpool), Petr Nedved (Lazio), Martin Frydek (Sparta Prague), Martin Cizek (Sparta Prague)
Attackers - Vladimir Smicer (Racing Lens), Pavel Kuka (Kaiserslautern), Horst Siegl (Sparta Prague), Vratislav Lokvenc (Sparta Prague)
